idea-plugin.name: Explain Code Audio
idea-plugin.description:
Right-click "Explain This (Audio)" to get a spoken, line-highlighted walkthrough of the selected code — or the method/class under the cursor. Uses Claude Code (headless) as the reasoning backbone and a local Kokoro TTS server for narration.

Requires the Claude CLI on PATH and a local TTS server (see the plugin's setup docs).

action.description: Audio-explain the selected code, the symbol under the cursor, or the selected file/folder
Open the per-engine narration settings: status, install Kokoro / language packs, Windows voices

fixtures/plans/scenes-tour.json: 5 frames in 3 scenes, 10 steps, 3 rebuilds. The tree is REPLACED at steps 5, 8 and 10 and stands still everywhere else. Step 10 returns to scene 0, which is rebuilt rather than restored

action.text: 2 — Load: One method as a one-node tree
action.description: fixtures/plans/single-frame.json: 1 frame, 3 steps, one in-file arrow. The commonest shape there is, and the case round 3 judged as good as the in-place surface it replaced

action.text: 3 — Load: Links — one scene, wide, deep, cross-frame
action.description: fixtures/plans/tree-links.json: 5 frames (3 siblings + a grandchild) in ONE scene, 10 steps, four cross-frame relations. The subject for the portal-pair work, and the regression control: a plan that never mentions scenes must render with 0 rebuilds

action.text: 4 — Load: Five links on one line (the routing fan)
action.description: fixtures/plans/link-fan.json: 3 root nodes, 6 steps, FIVE links per step. Steps 1-2 are five token links off one row, diving then rising, two of them landing on one far row; step 3 is five line-end links off one row; steps 4-5 are three same-editor links plus two portals off one row, at line level then token level; step 6 is five links off five DIFFERENT pairs of rows, which is the routing staircase. No nesting anywhere in it, so what is judged is the routing and nothing else

fixtures/plans/plan2-occurrence.json: 1 frame, 7 steps, every one anchored on a token that occurs more than once in its own range. Steps 1-2 and 3-4 are pairs on ONE line (plain and dotted); step 5 counts across two lines; step 7 asks for one occurrence past the end, which must cost the pulse and nothing else

fixtures/plans/plan3-unresolvable.json: 1 frame, 7 steps. Absent, wrong case, outside the range, blank, and one that resolves only on the substring pass — each beside a control that succeeds. First and last steps resolve, so a run that stopped pulsing partway is visible
Entry 3's plan with frame 2's callLine set to 140, a line its parent does not keep. Expect [warn] frame.call-line-not-kept, and frame 2 rendered at top level WITH its own child still nested inside it

action.text: 8 — Load: Parent in another scene (failure path)
action.description: Entry 1's plan with frame 3 moved to scene 2, where its parent has no node. Expect [warn] frame.parent-other-scene and scene 2 showing TWO top-level nodes — degraded, not dropped

action.text: 9 — Load: Over the line budget (pressure path)
action.description: Entry 3's plan with the root frame keeping the rest of its file: 88 kept lines against the cap of 60. The extreme rather than the only case — the fold now runs on every step whatever the budget says, and two of the other fixtures are over the cap on their own. Expect [info] scene.line-budget-exceeded, and a step touching one handler collapsing the nestings it does not touch

action.text: 10 — Load: Beats (PLAY this one, do not step)
action.description: fixtures/plans/plan4-beats.json: 1 frame, 7 steps. A beat with a `say` fires off the playback clock, so Next/Previous shows no pulse for steps 1-4 — press Play. Step 1 is three beats on three lines; step 2 three beats on one line; step 3 is the "e.g." split, where a sentence NUMBER would land wrong; step 4 puts two beats in one sentence and only the first may fire; step 5 is one pulse and no timing; step 6 is a five-line callout; step 7 is the LEGACY shape — a bare token over two ranges, with the token in the second, which is the case that used to resolve to nothing
Advance one plan step. No TTS involved, so a round can judge what is drawn without a narration server
Stop the walkthrough: the tree tab closes. Read the editor count after this — a scene change releases and creates editors on every crossing, so a leak would compound here
